mishnah-berurah/1:א: (1) By candlelight — on the night of the 14th, when people are in their homes and candlelight is then good for checking, unlike by day when light does not shine as at night; the Sages fixed checking specifically by candlelight so one can check also in holes and cracks. If he checked early on the 13th by candlelight, he must return and check on the night of the 14th per the Sages' enactment; nevertheless it appears one should not bless then on bedikat chametz, for some hold b'dieved he fulfilled with the first checking. However, if he checked on the night of the 13th by candlelight — at night candlelight is good for checking — and was very careful not to bring chametz, he need not check again — most Acharonim agree; one who wishes to be stringent and check again should at least not bless then.
mishnah-berurah/1:ב: (2) And if he passed — but l'chatchila it is forbidden to postpone checking to the day of the 14th, as above.
mishnah-berurah/1:ג: (3) But by candlelight — through it he can search well in hiding places, holes, and cracks.
mishnah-berurah/1:ד: (4) And a portico — a place with three walls and a roof, with great light through a fourth side completely open.
mishnah-berurah/1:ה: (5) If he checked by sunlight — this too refers when he passed and did not check on the night of the 14th and checks on the 14th; for a portico whose light is great he need not use a candle, sunlight suffices. Shulchan Aruch's b'dieved language is because l'chatchila even a portico requires checking on the night of the 14th. It is explained in Shas that one who did not check at night and checks by day checks in the morning because the diligent precede mitzvot, and he should not eat before checking (Acharonim).
mishnah-berurah/1:ו: (6) It suffices — regarding whether one may check on the 13th by its light: l'chatchila forbidden, he must wait for the night of the 14th; b'dieved it appears he need not check again — see Magen Avraham end of siman who wrote nevertheless one should return and check at least one room at night — see there.
mishnah-berurah/1:ז: (7) Opposite the skylight in a room — skylight means what is in the middle of the roof; likewise opposite windows in walls; specifically opposite skylight and window itself where light is great, unlike from the sides where there is also light but not like a portico; even opposite the window itself — only when there is no glass; with glass, its law is like the sides.
mishnah-berurah/2:א: (8) By torchlight — one cannot put it into holes and cracks, and one fears lest he burn the house and not check well; one does not check with wooden torches (called kiyin) whose light is also great like a torch.
mishnah-berurah/2:ב: (9) And not with a tallow candle — fearing it may drip on vessels and ruin them.
mishnah-berurah/2:ג: (10) And not of oil — fearing to put it into holes and cracks lest oil spill. B'dieved if he checked by torchlight the checking does not count and he must return with a single candle; tallow and fat candles count b'dieved; regarding oil there are opinions among Acharonim whether it counts b'dieved.
mishnah-berurah/2:ד: (11) But with a wax candle — if he has no wax he may check with those candles that b'dieved suffice (Acharonim).
mishnah-berurah/2:ה: (12) Even braided — meaning all the more if glued together it is considered a torch; but even braided one might think it is like one candle — he teaches otherwise (Magen Avraham); from Peri Megadim it implies whatever he holds together in his hand without separating is a torch; a candle with two wicks as sometimes made in tallow candles — if there is space between wicks it is a torch (there).
mishnah-berurah/3:א: (13) Where there is concern chametz was brought — not only places regularly used with chametz, which obviously require checking, but even where chametz is not regularly used all year, only where there is concern chametz was brought there incidentally — also requires checking, as explained below.
mishnah-berurah/3:ב: (14) All rooms of the house — even rooms used for pledges where sometimes one enters mid-meal to return a pledge to its owner, lest he forgot bread there; likewise similar cases such as cellars where fruits, preserves, and cheeses are stored, entered mid-meal to take them; likewise wood storage and coal, for the servant enters mid-meal for candles to light and wood for cooking.
mishnah-berurah/3:ג: (15) That bread is not suspected — in places where bread is not suspected, sometimes one enters mid-meal with bread in hand to bring more wine for his meal; likewise storehouses of other drinks where they regularly drink — require checking.
mishnah-berurah/3:ד: (16) From them — storehouses where he takes from them and has a fixed practice to take at once what he needs for a meal — no checking, since they are not accustomed to enter mid-meal (Acharonim).
mishnah-berurah/3:ה: (17) Do not require checking — presumably chametz is not brought unless he knows chametz was brought.
mishnah-berurah/3:ו: (18) Require checking — because they are regularly used and there is concern a little chametz remained.
mishnah-berurah/4:א: (19) Less than three handbreadths — presumably they were not used; but if he knows chametz was used there that year, even a handbreadth requires checking. In a house where children are found on the 13th, checking is required lest children left a little chametz.
mishnah-berurah/4:ב: (20) Do not require checking — on oven tops regularly used, checking is required; obviously all holes around them require checking.
mishnah-berurah/5:ב: (22) And the tower — called alma'or or similar; they used slanted roofs; but like ours with level roofs where people use them — checking required; all the more inside the tower if chametz is sometimes used, or things taken mid-meal — certainly requires checking.
mishnah-berurah/5:ג: (23) Their roofs are unfit — their house roofs were level and regularly used on them — checking required. Our ceilings under a slanted roof — if regularly used, checking required, for sometimes one goes mid-meal with bread in hand, as seif 3. Where effort is great, it appears one may be lenient by selling that place to a non-Jew together with chametz there.
mishnah-berurah/6:א: (24) Chicken coop — likewise floor of house where chickens are found — no checking; nevertheless sweep under beds, for sometimes a large piece of chametz is dragged there by chickens that they cannot eat, or another reason. Where they eat all year and no chickens — all agree check under benches and tables where chametz commonly falls; some say even with chickens, if they ate chametz close to Pesach it is like definite chametz — impossible chametz did not fall on the ground, and chickens' eating does not remove certainty — checking required as law.
mishnah-berurah/6:ב: (25) Middle of courtyard — not specifically middle — same law for sides of courtyard; it comes to exclude only holes in sides of courtyard that require checking.
mishnah-berurah/6:ג: (26) But definite chametz — for definite chametz we do not rely on this — checking required, for doubt does not remove certainty; all the more where they place geese in their coop and put outside a vessel with oat and barley stalks — kernels fall outside and they cannot eat there — definitely requires checking, for this is real chametz when kernels are soaked in water (Chayei Adam).
mishnah-berurah/6:ד: (27) No — see Magen Avraham: his view is chametz brought long before Pesach, guarded close to Pesach that chametz not fall — no checking; perhaps all thirty days are called close to Pesach; Mekor Chayim holds only what was on the night of the 14th after checking time arrived — then we do not rely birds will eat; but what was definitely before that is not called definite chametz — no checking.
mishnah-berurah/6:ה: (28) But below — Acharonim elaborated to resolve the contradiction; for halacha several agree: in one's courtyard or partners' courtyard it is forbidden to throw chametz relying ravens will eat; b'dieved if thrown, must check and destroy; but ownerless place for many, like a street — permitted to throw chametz and declare it ownerless before prohibition time; if ravens did not eat and it remains after prohibition time, we are not concerned since it left his possession — like selling to a non-Jew before prohibition time.
mishnah-berurah/7:א: (29) And the rest he nullifies in his heart — lest it rolled into the hole. Even if definite chametz was there, nullification also helps — not like hiding in a pit since he does not act with hands — see siman 436 whether benefit is permitted from such chametz after Pesach.
mishnah-berurah/7:ב: (30) Lest he say sorcery — in what he searches at night by candle in holes; nevertheless tomorrow on the 14th he checks by daylight so a non-Jew will not suspect him.
mishnah-berurah/7:ג: (31) Comes to danger — although agents of a mitzvah are not harmed where harm is common it is different; even though they exempted from night checking for this reason, nullification is still required; Acharonim wrote even definite chametz need not be checked at night but by day in daylight, and we certainly require nullification here, as above.
mishnah-berurah/8:א: (32) Used with chametz — meaning regularly used, not known that chametz is there now.
mishnah-berurah/8:ב: (33) Even if not three handbreadths for a dog to dig — meaning still within dog-digging height, smell reaches three handbreadths; we might fear a dog will dig during Pesach and reveal it — nevertheless no checking required, etc.
mishnah-berurah/8:ג: (34) Need not check — nevertheless must nullify in heart lest chametz be there and he transgress; if he did not nullify until after prohibition time, world practice on Shabbat is he must search with hoe and shovel — see Beit Meir: Rashi and Ran agree; Tosafot are doubtful — see there.
mishnah-berurah/8:ד: (35) Scorpion danger — specifically where scorpions are found; perhaps where snakes are found one must check, for harm is not so common (Magen Avraham and Eshel Avraham); see siman 104 what we wrote regarding snakes that kill — law like scorpions.
mishnah-berurah/8:ה: (36) After he finishes his checking — during checking, even searching for a needle, he is an agent of a mitzvah and not harmed, like one who says "this rock for charity that my sons live" — completely righteous even if he also intends his benefit.
mishnah-berurah/8:ו: (37) Must remove it — if he did not and Pesach passed, forbidden even though he nullified, like all chametz he transgressed on Pesach — siman 448 seif 5.
mishnah-berurah/8:ז: (38) He nullifies in his heart — nullification is d'rabbanan lest he open the mound on the festival and transgress "it shall not be seen"; d'oraisa he does not transgress at all — only hiding with hands is d'oraisa forbidden; but here since the mound fell on him automatically he does not transgress. Some say d'oraisa he must nullify, otherwise even without intent to open on the festival he transgresses "it shall not be found" like hiding l'chatchila; per their view if he did not nullify until after prohibition time he must open the mound to destroy since not in his power to nullify; but if a large mound fell impossible to open and lost from him and everyone — all permit, for we do not call it "yours."
mishnah-berurah/8:ח: (39) And it suffices — if after Pesach the mound was opened and chametz revealed, it is permitted even to eat, for chametz he transgressed on Pesach is not forbidden except rabbinic penalty for transgressing "it shall not be seen" and "it shall not be found" d'oraisa or d'rabbanan as explained siman 448; here he did not transgress at all — not fit to penalize.
mishnah-berurah/9:א: (40) Cellar where rows are arranged — specifically cellar used for meal needs where sometimes the servant goes mid-meal with bread to bring wine to the table and forgets bread there (Acharonim).
mishnah-berurah/9:ב: (41) Need not check — see Biur Halacha.
mishnah-berurah/9:ג: (42) And not the entire cellar area — meaning need not check all upper rows seeing the ceiling along length and width — only the last row opposite the entrance seeing ceiling and entrance together, and another barrel row below seeing only the entrance.
mishnah-berurah/10:_: (43) Require checking — on night of 14th by candle; shamashim are not careful to check at night but sweep well by day — not proper; they must be warned to fulfill the Sages' mitzvah properly and may bless on this bedika; but need not nullify afterward since they cannot nullify chametz not theirs. If he passed and did not check synagogues and study halls on night of 14th, he may check them l'chatchila on the 14th by daylight without candle, since they have many windows and great light — law like portico in seif 1 (Acharonim); per s.k. 7 if windows have glass, even opposite window is not like portico — when checking by sunlight he must open windows.
mishnah-berurah/11:א: (44) And intending — not only without presumption of sweeping, but even if intending for bedika sweeping does not help.
mishnah-berurah/11:ב: (45) Nevertheless must check — sweeping is not complete bedika lest chametz remain in a crevice; even if he checked holes and cracks by candle he must return at night like all Israel, not to divide bedika from bedika (all explained from Turei Zahav in Mordechai); per seif 1 in Biur Halacha one may not rely on daytime checking even by candle, for candle does not shine by day as at night.
mishnah-berurah/11:ג: (46) Must clean his rooms — one does not check well without cleaning; custom to clean whole house on the 13th so bedika can be done properly at start of night of 14th, as siman 431 seif 1; at bedika time custom to take feathers and clean well in holes and cracks to drag chametz with the feather.
mishnah-berurah/11:ד: (47) That they sometimes place chametz — even if he says "I am certain I did not place chametz" — a matter not dependent on him and not in his awareness — therefore checking required; world practice only shakes pockets at biur time — correct to check at bedika time; nevertheless shake again at biur lest he returned and put chametz from what he ate after bedika (Acharonim).
mishnah-berurah/11:ה: (48) Require checking — both his own and children's in the house.
